purpose: Freeze the target authority and responsibility boundary for the ConfigData Lookup reset without modifying the validated Stage 0-6 lookup/index baseline or prematurely cutting over legacy Stage 7/8 Project Doctor orchestration.

owns: Read already-materialized ConfigData Lookup indices and dependency metadata.
Resolve ID locator lookups through the frozen Stage 0-6 materialized layers.
Return materialized direct/reverse reference results without transitive inference.
Perform bounded literal find operations supported by the existing CLI contract.
Determine lookup/index freshness from explicit dependency metadata and source hashes.
Report missing, malformed, or stale lookup materialization as a lookup-owned failure.
Perform explicit lookup/index materialization only through a separately invoked writer/rebuild operation after CLR5 separation.
doesNotOwn: Hero, Soldier, Equipment, Banner, Skin, or other domain semantic authority.
Discovery of new semantic relations or recomputation of frozen canonical relations.
Domain semantic fan-out from ConfigData changes.
Selection or execution authority for Hero, Soldier, Equipment, Banner, or other page validators.
Selection or execution authority for Route/Hosted QA or Browser/UI QA.
Cross-domain mutation, frontend mutation, asset mutation, deployment mutation, status-source mutation, or Project Status mutation.
Filename-similarity inference, name JOIN, ID arithmetic, or transitive impact inference.
Silent fallback to raw ConfigData when materialized lookup data is stale or missing.

legacyStage7And8Disposition.note: CLR1 freezes what the reset ConfigData Lookup will and will not own. It does not falsely declare Stage 7/8 physically retired before the later cutover step.

reviews.detail: The dedicated configdata-lookup Project Check owner and validator are intentionally deferred to CLR4.

Stage 7/8 Project Doctor orchestration files are preserved during CLR1. Their active authority/runtime dependency is removed only after the independent replacement passes parity and admission gates in CLR7.
The existing Stage 6 workflow writer capability remains unchanged in CLR1; required validation/write separation belongs to CLR5.

validation.reason: CLR1 changes only the reset authority contract and does not modify lookup implementation, generated lookup data, semantic data, frontend, assets, deployment, or hosted/browser behavior.

nextStart: Begin CLR2 from this frozen boundary. Create the independent tools/configdata-lookup namespace as an adapter/entrypoint over the validated Stage 0-6 materialized artifacts without rewriting the Stage 0-6 producers, changing CLI semantics, or inheriting Stage 7/8 Project Doctor orchestration.
reopenConditions: Authoritative Stage 0-6 evidence contradicts the CLR0 frozen baseline.
A required core Lookup capability cannot be preserved without raw ConfigData fallback or semantic recomputation.
New authoritative evidence proves a cross-domain orchestration responsibility is intrinsic to ConfigData Lookup rather than Project Check or another owning tool.
The target read/write separation cannot preserve required lookup/index materialization behavior within a bounded owning scope.
